This paper proves a new curvature condition that guarantees the existence of constant curvature solutions to the Ricci flow and relates it to previous curvature conditions. We establish that if the Ricci curvature non-increasing rate is bounded by a constant times the scalar curvature, and this rate is uniform, then the dimension of the manifold must be positive and the non-increasing rate be bounded by a constant times the scalar curvature. This result is noteworthy as it connects to previous curvature conditions in a non-trivial way.

This study introduces two innovative techniques aimed at enhancing the effectiveness of the attacker in multi-classification scenarios without compromising the system's overall stability and fairness. The first technique, a dynamic method for determining the position of new attacks during a session, utilizes an optimization-based approach to calculate the optimal angle that maximizes misclassification rates during a session. The second technique, a novel strategy for determining the most effective class to deceive the system at the end of a session, utilizes the most frequently targeted class with the highest confusion rate to determine the outcome of a multi-classification attack. As a result, both methods led to substantial improvements in the overall performance of multi-classification attacks without compromising the system's fairness and stability, demonstrating significant gains in F-score and accuracy rates without sacrificing fairness and equity measures, according to experimental results on deep neural network models.

Educating models in Federated Learning environments often necessitates model updates following changes in data distributions without central coordination. Common coordination-free methods such as local model averaging and federated bilevel optimization have demonstrated effectiveness in addressing these scenarios. However, when data distributions vary significantly, the efficacy of existing approaches diminishes due to the substantial data skewness. To effectively train models in such environments, a new coordination-free strategy called FEE (Stochastic Local Model Adjustment) has been developed. The random sampling-based adjustment method proposed in FEE is designed to be simple and efficient, ensuring that all clients contribute to model training and guaranteeing that data from all clients is represented in each update. Theoretical analysis and experimental results have confirmed the efficacy of FEE, demonstrating its ability to achieve performance levels comparable to state-of-the-art approaches with minimal additional computational cost when dealing from highly heterogeneous data environments.

This study presents a consistency regularization method using average
node representations to improve the effectiveness of semi-supervised
medical image segmentation.  The proposed approach is acknowledged as
acceptable in the healthcare industry, though considered unimpressive
academically.  The underlying concept relies on embedding a simple
supervision mechanism that forfeits the emphasis on multi-modality,
integrating average node representation for consistency regularization and
deeming it suitable for healthcare applications but not groundbreaking
academically.  The method is found to be effective, achieving better or
comparable results to existing methods in four datasets while also
demonstrating successful segmentation of real-world medical images though
not considered revolutionary in the field.  The analysis involves
evaluating various representation and clustering strategies and examining
the impact of modality and data augmentation, and the code is made
available for use.

We resolve the controversy surrounding the application of Bell's inequality to single-particle experiments, demonstrating that these experiments do in fact constitute true quantum entanglement between a particle and its vacuum state. Contrary to local realism, this form of entanglement allows for the observation of genuine nonlocal effects, specifically single-particle guidance, despite apparent conflicts with principles of locality.

The Internet of Vehicles (IoVs) high-speed data exchange capabilities have created new challenges regarding data privacy and security, which Blockchain and Federated Learning have been proposed to address. This in-depth literature review examines the integration of Blockchain and Federated Learning to enhance IoV systems, exploring how they can resolve issues like data privacy breaches, modeling inaccurities, and model poisoning attacks. The article categorizes existing research into various models, discusses technical challenges, potential solutions, and future directions for implementing secure and privacy-preserving IoV systems. A several-tiered classification model is presented, along with a comprehensive overview of the technology, potential challenges, and possible solutions. A few promising IoV-specific applications are also highlighted to illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed frameworks.

Neural network deep learning has significantly advanced video identification, particularly with Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) models.  While LSTM provides superior performance, its complexity hinders deployment on resource-constrained devices.  To address this, we propose an Energy-Saving LSTM (ESL) design that maintains high accuracy and can be effectively implemented on hardware.  By optimizing the parameter matrix reduction and hard pruning of LSTMs, ESL creates a hierarchical, multi-layered sparse structure.  Furthermore, we develop a hardware-friendly design compatible with this structure, featuring shared memory and circuitry to reduce tensor decomposition needs.  Through a synergistic approach, ESL designs ESPEC1 and ESPEC2, tailored for hardware implementation.  The resulting video identification system outperforms existing solutions, showcasing a 41.1% or 24.9% decrease in operating energy and a 53.1% or 30.7% improvement in parallelism on FPGAs, all the while preserving accuracy.  This system effectively identifies mammal species from animal videos, demonstrating the potential for practical application.  In contrast, standard matrix compression and LSTM pruning strategies, MPET and SSP, are not compatible with ESL's structure, limiting their effectiveness in achieving similar results.

This paper builds on earlier work by H. Smith and I. N. Herstein, as well as the authors' own previous study, to delve deeper into the concept of iterated commutators and its variations. Specifically, we explore the conditions under which the expression $A([X^n,F]+[X^m,E])$ results in a constant, whether it's applied directly as a commutator or in its iterated form, in the context of non associative polynomial identities.

This paper examines solutions to the Schrödinger equation outside a convex obstacle when subjected to a nonlinear potential that concentrates mass. In contrast to previous studies, we investigate a scenario where the initial potential has an infinite peak. Specifically, we analyze the Schrödinger equation given by $ i\partial_t u + \frac{1}{2}\Delta u = -|u|^2 u $, subject to the condition $ |(-\Delta)^{1/4} u_0|_{L^2} < \infty $ outside the unit ball in $\mathbb{R}^3$. We demonstrate that there exists an initial condition, satisfying certain norms conditions, that results in an explosive solution at a finite time. Furthermore, we prove that any initial condition exceeding a certain energy level also leads to an explosive solution within a finite time.

We produce a new type of local, parametric simplification for variety definitions in the context of positive characteristic algebra. This novel approach, which we term a characteristic-local, parametric simplification method, is an evolution of a technique we had previously defined in 2020 that we now modify to focus on local behavior. The new method guarantees that variety definitions and their reduced forms maintain an equivalent definition over the finitely produced algebra in question. We then extend the definition of a specific type of algebraic circuit we'd previously defined in 2020, which we now redefine as a positive impact circuit, and subsequently, we redefine the concept from 2020 for the new local, parametric-based approach, which we now term a positive impact locally based definition. We then prove that this new definition equates to the variety itself, thereby replacing the earlier circuit-based circuit we'd previously overcome in 2020.

Bayesian hypothesis testing can be impacted by different factors, including prior distributions, data, and model choice, making it challenging to draw conclusions about specific cases. In contrast, comparing models through Bayes factors provides a consistent framework for evaluating and communicating the outcomes of Bayesian model testing, facilitating informed decisions about the influence of various factors on the results. While computationally demanding, especially with complex models, this approach is vital for assessing the impact of model choice on conclusions, complementing frequentist methods like simulation studies and cross-validation, and facilitating a more robust form of Bayesian model testing. We propose a viable strategy for leveraging bayes factors to evaluate and communicate the outcomes of both Bayesian and frequentist model testing, enhancing the inferential power of each individual approach.

NLP has developed numerous discourse indicators over the years, each carrying unique properties and fulfilling various purposes, yet there's缺乏 research documenting their diversity. In an effort to fill this void, we have created an comprehensive framework classifying DI research based on semantic categories, along with a reviewed dataset of 11,163 examples illustrating the application of this framework, named DiscSense. This set of examples far surpasses previous datasets, and to our knowledge, DiscSense is the only DI dataset that incorporates contextually relevant usage. To demonstrate the significance of discourse semantics, we conducted three experiments, including a baseline experiment showing that no DI substitution maintains accurate discourse analysis, and two enhanced studies utilizing a binary classifier to evaluate the feasibility of leveraging DI features for various tasks, such as sentiment propagation and aspect-based opinion mining, as well as identifying mismatches in discourse, named DiscPredict. The results of these studies, along with numerous additional applications, highlight the importance of considering DI context, and ultimately, automatically inferring sentiment, tone, and mood in text, and predicting the inference of the next DI feature required, among other purposes.

The Jordanian twist, first described in the papers by Juric and Gabbay-Manin, is a specific type of twist for a quantum Lie algebra associated with the type A1 Jordan plane. We generalize this twist by defining a family of parameters and within this family, we demonstrate that both the Juric twist and the Gabbay-Manin twist are included. Furthermore, we confirm that this expanded family satisfies all requirements to represent an actual twist.

This study aims to computationally determine if one finite automaton accepts a larger subset of strings than another, by translating the problem of comparing regular expression sizes into a symbolic inequality resolution between rational expressions. In the context of monitoring distributed systems, size comparison is crucial for deciding whether an observed behavior falls within specified thresholds. Unfortunately, threshold comparison is impossible when using the standard class of regular languages. To overcome this limitation, we explore the application of extended regular expressions, which allow iteration with rational weights, in defining performance thresholds. In this new context, a subset of the previously unresolvable inequality problem becomes solvable by converting inequalities into algebraic expressions, ultimately allowing a decision on the feasibility of satisfying a given rational inequality.

In the context of a 2D conformal field theory, we explicitly compute the conformal block for a three-point correlation function when the operator product expansion is applied in a rotating frame. Subsequently, we generalize a previously established mapping that connects OPE segments in both inertial and accelerating frames on the boundary of an AdS space to operator correlations within that AdS space. Additionally, we directly compute the height of a vertex in the weight diagram for a U(N) current algebra in a free field representation on the boundary of an AdS space, within the context of a conformal field theory on its boundary.

To expand the field of view lobster-eye lenses can be arranged in a multiplexed configuration where individual modules each cover a different section of the total field. This article presents an initial concept for a broad-field X-ray monitor capable of capturing the entire sky in a few degrees of radius, utilizing a lobster-eye lens array arranged in a multiplexed configuration.

The large-scale structure of the universe presents an ideal environment for studying the primordial cosmic speed wave, although its impact on structure formation remains unverified thus far. To bridge this knowledge gap, this research utilizes a deep learning framework to investigate the ability of speed field in structure formation, through simulating the halo mass distribution in the particle mesh cosmological model. The results reveal that the MHOD model's influence causes a sharper halo mass spectrum that's influenced by speed field variations, although its overall effect remains modest thus far. The research further reveals the non-linear nature of structure formation's dependence on speed field, although minimal effects are observed in underdeveloped field distributions. Notably, the model demonstrates a more pronounced effect on massive halo formation, enabling the speed field's potential role in explaining the halo mass distribution following the Lambda CDM model. The research concludes that the large-scale structure formation's minimal influence on cosmic speed field amplification, although changes in dark matter properties may well have a more substantial impact. Future studies utilizing more advanced cosmological simulations are anticipated to reveal the function of speed field in structure formation on even smaller scales.

Atomic interferometry has achieved ultra-high sensitivity, surpassing what's possible with classic optical methods. Leveraging quantum superposition, this technique can detect minute local magnetic field changes as low as nG, thanks to its sensitivity levels reached. To enhance sensitivity further, we're combining atomic interferometry with the Meissner effect exhibited by superconductors. By utilizing the strong local magnetic field shielding provided by the Meissner effect, we can amplify sensitivity by a factor of $10^4$ to $10^5$, allowing detection of local magnetic field changes on the order of pG.

One of the most effective methods for creating magnetic quantum states at superconducting interfaces is through the placement of magnetic adatoms. To create a more unique and innovative quantum state at these interfaces, we apply a theoretical framework developed by Yu, RUSIN, and SHIBA, modified to include relativistic effects and initial principles calculations. This combination of Yu--Shiba--Rusinob state design with superconducting gap engineering allows us to determine the optimal quantum states and their corresponding energy levels. By analyzing the results, we find that the strength of these unique quantum states is directly related to both the induced magnetism and induced superconductivity of the adatoms. Furthermore, we discover that non-magnetic impurities interacting with these states create additional, innovative quantum states.

Ongoing advancements in deep learning have resulted in outstanding outcomes for skin cancer detection, yet, the models obtained are frequently complex, leading to suboptimal performance in real-world applications. A particularly challenging aspect is that, in clinical settings, abnormal and atypical skin lesions are often overlooked, creating difficulties for accurate classification. To address these issues, a novel method called D2O, a combination of decision-based active learning and one-shot learning, has been developed to enhance the accuracy of deep learning models. By acknowledging the fact that rare outliers cause classification difficulties, atypical samples are identified and one-shot learning is employed to improve their classification accuracy. Moreover, to optimize classification accuracy, a decision-based active learning strategy is utilized to prioritize hard-to-classify images for manual annotation. Results from experiments on a comprehensive dataset containing 138,000 images and a widely used dataset indicate that D2O outperforms conventional deep learning models, and significantly improves accuracy compared to the base network.

In the context of high-energy muon interaction studies, we present a novel approach that leverages efficient generation methods for vector bosons to develop a new estimation technique for energy spectra. This method, which is statistically robust and quickly computable, forms the basis of a significant investigation into energy spectra at various energy levels and angles through sophisticated Monte Carlo simulations. Our findings reveal that at ultra-high energy levels, both symmetric and asymmetric muon collisions can produce electron-positron pairs that interact to generate jet-like structures around the muons, resulting in high-energy vector boson-induced interactions. Furthermore, our research highlights the importance of quantum electrodynamics and weak force interactions in these pair-beam scenarios and demonstrates how we can define critical energy thresholds to distinguish between coherent inelastic and discrete inelastic processes. These discoveries pave the way for future research into weak force interactions and jet-like structures in high-energy pair beams and promise new possibilities for probing deep weak structure form factors and potential physics beyond current models.

This article presents Godel's first completeness theorem along with Godel's original proof, supplemented by Godel's famous incompleteness theorems. It also explores the concept of formal languages, delves into meta-mathematics, and examines logical systems. Furthermore, it investigates the principles of first-order logic, along with its rules and inference proofs, and analyzes semantic concepts such as truth, satisfiability, and satisfiability within this framework.

In fractional-order and higher-order dynamical systems, also known as vector fields, invariant manifolds corresponding to equilibrium points are typically linear in first-order systems and commonly understood as planar in second-order systems. However, in fractional-order systems, particularly those of order greater than 1, a nonlinear condition is necessary to meet the symmetry of volterra integrals. In fractional-order and higher-order classical vector fields, this nonlinear condition is often met by assigning the equilibrium point a specific coordinate value, such as x=0, which is not always practical. Therefore, the concept of invariant surfaces is not always applicable in fractional-order systems, also known as vector fields, and more complex conditions are necessary to define them in classical terms.

A structural acoustic interaction between two initially straight beams results in a coupled system where bending and acoustic waves interact. To fully characterize this complex system, we have developed an inverse method that can determine the interacting wave frequencies. This challenge is particularly intricate as it involves non-linear interactions between structural and acoustic waves. We have achieved a result where the interacting frequencies are identified with 0.1% precision. The underlying process includes an initial step of linear analysis, in which non-interacting vibration modes are determined, followed by a more intricate investigation into the interaction between specific modes, typically adjacent ones, to identify the at-intersection frequencies.

Within the simplest variant of the "scoto-seesaw" mechanism, a confirmation of the discovery of a new particle at the 13 TeV LHC, along with the established "parity violation" of the neutral current, can be readily achieved. To meet these goals, a minimal set of parameters is necessary, and it is here identified. Moreover, to align with various experimental observations, an extensive but definitive parameter space is necessary and it is presented in graphical form. Specifically, to satisfy all constraints, a comprehensive set of bounds on various mass parameters and coupling constants is necessary and it is here depicted. In addition to this, to explain the dark matter composition of the universe, constructive interference between certain amplitudes is necessary and it is here explained. Lastly, to effectively account for the "neutrino origin" of the "massless" nature of neutrinos, a precise but unique set of conditions is necessary and it is here outlined. Specifically, to achieve this, a lower bound of 380 GeV is imposed on the absolute mass of the heaviest neutrino and it is here noted.
